::: {.tldr}
**Persistence**: a checkpointer saves the state after every step, so the agent remembers earlier turns and can resume later. **Streaming**: you see what the agent is doing while it works, message by message or token by token.
:::

## Reducer vs checkpointer

These two are easy to confuse. They work together.

| | Reducer (`operator.add`) | Checkpointer |
|---|---|---|
| Answers | *How* to combine updates | *Where* to keep the state between calls |
| Lasts | One `invoke` | Every call with the same `thread_id` |

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  C1["Call 1<br/>[] + [SF?]"] --> R1["… answer"]
  R1 -- "💾 saved under thread 1" --> C2["Call 2<br/>[SF?, …, answer] + [LA?]"]
  C2 --> R2["understands 'LA'"]
```

## Adding memory

```python
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver

memory = MemorySaver()     # in-memory: fine for learning, lost when the process stops

class Agent:
    def __init__(self, model, tools, checkpointer, system=""):
        ...
        self.graph = graph.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)
        ...

abot = Agent(model, [tool], system=prompt, checkpointer=memory)
```

## Threads

A **thread** is one conversation. Same `thread_id`: the history continues. New `thread_id`: a fresh start.

```python
thread = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}

abot.graph.invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage(content="What is the weather in SF?")]}, thread)
abot.graph.invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage(content="What about in LA?")]}, thread)   # remembers SF
```

## Two levels of streaming

::: {.concepts}
::: {.concept}
`graph.stream()`

One event per step: the tool request, the tool result, then the final answer.
:::
::: {.concept}
`graph.astream_events()`

One event per token, like a chat app typing. Asynchronous: use `async for`.
:::
:::

**Message by message:**

```python
for event in abot.graph.stream({"messages": messages}, thread):
    for v in event.values():
        print(v["messages"])
```

**Token by token:**

```python
async for event in abot.graph.astream_events({"messages": messages}, thread, version="v2"):
    if event["event"] == "on_chat_model_stream":
        content = event["data"]["chunk"].content
        if content:                 # empty while the model is requesting a tool
            print(content, end="|")
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Remember
- A checkpointer saves the state **after every node**: the basis for memory, resuming and human-in-the-loop.
- One `thread_id` per user or conversation keeps histories separate.
- `MemorySaver` is for demos. In production, use a database-backed checkpointer (SQLite, Postgres, Redis packages).
- Stream **messages** to show progress, stream **tokens** for a responsive answer.
:::

## Quiz

<details class="quiz">
<summary>You ask "Which one is warmer?" on a brand new thread. What happens?</summary>
<p>The agent has no history on that thread, so it doesn't know which places you mean and asks you to clarify.</p>
</details>

<details class="quiz">
<summary>Why are no tokens printed while the agent calls a tool?</summary>
<p>A tool request has empty <code>content</code>: it only holds a function call. Only the final answer contains text.</p>
</details>

<details class="quiz">
<summary>Does <code>operator.add</code> on its own give memory between two <code>invoke</code> calls?</summary>
<p>No. Each call starts from a fresh state. Only a checkpointer reloads the previous messages.</p>
</details>
